title: Exercise 3.3 · Q2
summary: Which of the following diagrams represent functions and of which type? > 🖼 Fig (1): left set {1, 2, 3},…
alt: Exercise 3.3 · Q2: Which of the following diagrams represent functions and of which type? > 🖼 Fig (1): left set {1, 2, 3}, right set {a, b, c, d}. Arrows: 1 → a, 1 → b, 2 → c, 3 → d. > 🖼 Fig (2): left set {a, b, c}, right set {1, 3, 5}. Arrows: a → 1, b → 3, c → 5. > 🖼 Fig (3): left set {1, 2, 3}, right set {a, b, c}. Arrows: 1 → a, 2 → b, 3 → c. > 🖼 Fig (4): left set {l, m, n}, right set {x, y, z}. Arrows: l → x, m → x, n → z (y receives no arrow).

steps.title: Solution
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{Fig }\mathbf{(1):}}\text{ the element }1\text{ is joined}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{to }\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{two}}\text{ elements (a and b). So }1\\[5pt]&\quad \text{has no unique image. This is }\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{not a}}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{function}\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{; it is only a relation.}}\\[5pt]&\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{Fig }\mathbf{(2):}}\text{ each of a, b, c has}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{exactly one image }(1,3,5),\text{ no two}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{elements have the same image, and}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{every element of the right set is}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{used. }\Rightarrow a\text{ function that is one-one and}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{onto, i.e. a }\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{bijective function}}\text{.}\\[5pt]&\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{Fig }\mathbf{(3):}}\text{ each of }1,2,3\text{ has}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{exactly one image (a, b, c), no}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{element of the right set is repeated,}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{and all of a, b, c are used. }\Rightarrow a\\[5pt]&\quad \textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{bijective function}}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{(one-one and onto).}\\[5pt]&\textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{Fig }\mathbf{(4):}}\text{ each of l, m, n has}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{exactly one image, so it is a}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{function. But l and m both go to x}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{(not one-one), and y is not an image}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{of any element (not onto). }\Rightarrow a\\[5pt]&\quad \textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{function from A into B}}\text{ that is}\\[5pt]&\quad \textcolor{#047857}{\textbf{not one-one}}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{(a many-one into function).}\end{aligned}\]
